raw_response:
I am 70 years old, I never went to school, and I have farmed these 6 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. I don't read books and I don't trust people who talk fancy — I watch my neighbors and I remember what happened last year.

This year I will plant 4 mu of spring maize and 2 mu of cotton, same as last year. Why change? The maize gave me about 550 kg per mu and the cotton about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu. Good enough. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends home money, so I can buy the inputs, but every yuan is still real money. I would rather spend too much on fertilizer than risk a thin harvest. A bad year means we eat corn porridge all winter.

For the maize, I buy hybrid seeds from the dealer in town — the same kind Old Wang from the east end of the village used, the one with cobs thick as a man's wrist. Before planting, I hire the rotary tiller for 30 yuan per mu to break up the soil. Then for each mu I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer, the kind that says 15-15-15 on the bag, that's 50 kg. I also throw 10 kg of superphosphate into the planting holes, and 5 kg of that white potash. When the corn is knee-high, I top-dress with half a bag of urea, 25 kg per mu. I know it is a lot, but three years ago I cut back and the leaves turned yellow before harvest. I lost money. Never again. I water three times: right after planting, when the tassels come out, and when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide twice — once when the little worms get into the heart of the plant, and once later if I see armyworms.

The cotton is on the 2 mu near the house. Cotton is greedy and it needs more work. I plant the improved cotton seeds with the big bolls. I put one bag of that 15-15-15 compound fertilizer on each mu, 50 kg, plus 15 kg of superphosphate and 8 kg of potash. Then I top-dress twice with urea — 20 kg when the first flowers open, and 15 kg more when the bolls are setting. That is a lot of nitrogen, but cotton will drop its flowers without it. I irrigate four times: planting, flowering, boll-setting, and once in August if the rain doesn't come. Cotton bollworm is the devil around here. I spray five times, starting when the squares show up, then every two weeks. I buy the cheap generic bottles from the dealer, not the expensive new names. I skip the fancy stuff because that money pays for the fertilizer instead.

I thought about cutting back because fertilizer prices went up again, but I saw that Old Zhang is putting on a full bag per mu, and so is everyone else in the village. If I do less, my field will look the worst. I do what I did last year. If the weather holds, I expect about 550 kg per mu from the maize and about 280 kg per mu of seed cotton.
